previous_catalog_record.summary: 0-bg grid (h~6-9, w~7-10) with 3 ACTIVE ROWS at rows 1, h//2, and h-2. Each active row has TWO COLORED CELLS in COLORS drawn from distinct_colors(3): cell at (r, idx+1) = colors[idx], cell at (r, w-2) = colors[(idx+1) % 3]. Other rows are BLANK (all 0). Rule (ROW-FIRST-COLOR FILL): for EACH ROW, scan LEFT-TO-RIGHT for the FIRST NONZERO CELL. If FOUND, FILL the ENTIRE ROW with that color (every cell in that row gets the first-encountered color). If the row is entirely 0, keep it 0. Net: each row collapses to its leftmost color; blank rows stay blank.

scope: Accepted generator repair; finite reviewer evidence, no new maintainer execution

sequential_dependency.intermediate: The full row-filled grid produced from the input, including the selected color of every originally nonblank row and zeros for every blank row.
sequential_dependency.step_a: For each input row, select its leftmost nonzero seed color and fill the entire row with that color; blank rows remain blank.
sequential_dependency.step_b: For each blank row, find the nearest nonblank row above and below in the row-filled intermediate and fill the gap only when those two intermediate colors are equal.
sequential_dependency.why_b_depends_on_a: The bridge decision and its output color are computed from nearest colors in Step A’s row-filled grid; changing Step A to rightmost seeds changes both which gaps qualify and the final filled colors.
